newsitem.title: FRANCE: LVMH 96 net seen weighed by exceptionals.
newsitem.headline: LVMH 96 net seen weighed by exceptionals.

text.p: French luxury goods group LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton is expected to report a drop in 1996 profit including exceptional items but a six percent increase if exceptionals are stripped out, analysts say.
LVMH, which is due to report its results early on Thursday, said last month that its provisional net attributable operating result would be up six percent over the 1995 level.

The group reported net attributable profit of 4,047 million francs for 1995 but one analyst calculated that the strictly comparable 1995 figure, that is, excluding exceptionals, would be 4,197 million francs.

A consensus forecast compiled by consultants Jacques Chahine Finance shows the market expects net attributable profit excluding exceptionals of 4.28 billion francs for 1996. Analysts' estimates range from 4.12 to 4.53 billion francs.
That figure would not include a 650 million franc extraordinary charge that LVMH said was due mainly to the impact of its sale last year of a third of its shares in British drinks group Guinness.
One analyst estimated LVMH's net attributable, including exceptional items, at 3.7 billion francs, down from last year.
The analyst said he expected a four to five percent drop in operating profit from 7,206 million francs for 1995 due to weakness in the perfume and cognac businesses last year.

LVMH in January reported a 4.6 percent rise in 1996 sales to 31.14 billion francs, but said cognac sales fell to 4.88 billion francs from 5.28 billion in 1995 and attributed the drop to weakness in Asian markets, namely Japan.

LVMH said it would use the Guinness stake sale to pay for part of its $2.6 billion acquisition of 61 percent of U.S. duty free chain DFS in January. The DFS acquisition will not be reflected in the 1996 results, analysts say.

But LVMH said in late February that, on a pro forma basis, the acquisition would have been "strongly positive at the net operating level before exceptional elements and writedown of goodwill" for 1996.

It said the acquisition would have a dilutive effect in its earnings per share (EPS) for 1997. EPS for 1996 is estimated at 50.2 francs, up from 47 francs for 1995, according to Jacques Chahine Finance. The firm's EPS estimates for LVMH for 1997 and 1998 are 55.5 francs and 63.3 francs, respectively.
LVMH will hold a news conference at 0800 GMT on Thursday morning for reporters and analysts to detail the results, which are due out at 0700 GMT.
